text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bloc launches campaign offensive: Bouchard attacks Charest at party rally as key sovereigntist leaders join forces.
- No vote planned for Zaire, rebels say: 'Re-education' top priority.
- Milgaard, officials agree to DNA test: Lab could destroy evidence in case.
- Chinese troops in Hong Kong try casual look: Blue berets part of Beijing's campaign to assure people they have nothing to fear.
- Bre-X sets reporters soul-searching: As dust from the salted gold-mines settles, business writers ask themselves what they missed and when.
- Delgratia says gold results fake: Consultant's review of Vancouver junior miner's Nevada exploration reveals tampering.
- Boardrooms buoyant about jobs: Firms expect to go on a hiring binge amid rosy business conditions: survey.
- Wall Street tosses coin on interest rates: Everyone's guessing as Fed meets today.
- Infrared connection unshackles wired world: By using invisible light, consumers won't have to fumble with cords to link their computers and telephones.
- Delgratia samples salted: Criminal investigation gets under way after forensic review shows samples from Josh gold deposit were tampered with and the company has been the victim of wrongdoing.
- Copyright move on photocopies will cost banks and lawyers dear.
- Amex puts a Tiger in its bank.
